properties.name: archone.messaging.core.enabled
properties.description: Whether to compose framework-neutral messaging defaults such as ChannelMapping, Clock, and Integration Event serde.

properties.name: archone.messaging.channels.mappings
properties.description: Logical channel to physical destination mappings. Unmapped channels use identity mapping; duplicate physical destinations fail startup.

properties.name: archone.messaging.jdbc.enabled
properties.description: Whether to adapt Spring JDBC and the application transaction manager to the framework-neutral messaging JDBC ports.

properties.name: archone.messaging.producer.jdbc.enabled
properties.description: Whether to compose the caller-transaction-required JDBC Outbox MessageProducer.

properties.name: archone.messaging.consumer.jdbc.enabled
properties.description: Whether to compose the JDBC Inbox duplicate detector and transactional idempotency decorator.

properties.name: archone.messaging.consumer.inbox-compatibility.enabled
properties.description: Whether to expose the temporary InboxRepo compatibility facade when its migration artifact is present. Gate I removes this path.

properties.name: archone.messaging.consumer.kafka.enabled
properties.description: Whether to compose the programmatic Spring Kafka MessageConsumer runtime.

properties.name: archone.messaging.consumer.groups
properties.description: Stable subscriber ID to Kafka consumer group mapping. Unmapped subscribers use the same value for both identities. Renaming a subscriber changes Inbox idempotency identity; renaming a group changes Kafka offset ownership and requires an explicit replay or cutover plan.

properties.name: archone.messaging.consumer.kafka.concurrency
properties.description: Default concurrency for programmatically created Kafka listener containers.

properties.name: archone.messaging.consumer.kafka.ack-mode
properties.description: Default Spring Kafka acknowledgement mode for programmatic subscriptions.

properties.name: archone.messaging.consumer.kafka.missing-topics-fatal
properties.description: Whether a programmatic subscription fails startup when a configured topic is missing.

properties.name: archone.messaging.consumer.kafka.observation-enabled
properties.description: Whether Spring Kafka transport observation is enabled for programmatic subscriptions; semantic consumer observation is configured separately.

properties.name: archone.messaging.consumer.kafka.shutdown-timeout
properties.description: Graceful shutdown timeout for programmatically created Kafka listener containers.

properties.name: archone.messaging.events.publisher.enabled
properties.description: Whether to expose the typed IntegrationEventPublisher when a MessageProducer exists.

properties.name: archone.messaging.events.dispatcher.enabled
properties.description: Whether to expose IntegrationEventDispatcherFactory when MessageConsumer and an explicit IntegrationEventNameMapping exist.

properties.name: archone.messaging.observation.enabled
properties.description: Whether messaging observations are composed when an ObservationRegistry bean exists. This does not select or install an exporter.

properties.name: archone.messaging.observation.producer.enabled
properties.description: Whether to observe synchronous Outbox append attempts through the producer interceptor lifecycle.

properties.name: archone.messaging.observation.consumer.enabled
properties.description: Whether to observe final semantic outcomes through the ordered consumer decorator chain.

properties.name: archone.messaging.flyway.enabled
properties.description: Whether to expose the namespaced MessagingFlywayFactory. This remains opt-in and never creates a Flyway initializer or changes an application schema by itself.

properties.name: archone.messaging.jpa.enabled
properties.description: Whether to compose temporary legacy JPA Outbox and Inbox facades when their compatibility artifacts are present.

properties.name: archone.messaging.jpa.register-package
properties.description: Whether to add the temporary legacy messaging JPA package to Spring Boot repository discovery. Disable when the application root already covers it.
